gloss: appoint; meet at a set time or place
summary: יָעַד is to fix a time or place, or to set a person apart for someone; in the niphal people meet or gather by such an arrangement, and Yahweh says he will meet with Israel at the tent. מוֹעֵד is what is so fixed: an appointed time, whether the seasons the lights mark, a day set beforehand, or Yahweh's own appointed times, the feasts of Leviticus 23; and the meeting or its place, above all the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד, the tent where Yahweh meets his people and speaks with them. עֵדָה is those who gather so, Israel assembled before Yahweh or any company, and the Peshitta's word for the church (Mat 16:18) is the same word. Arabic and Sabaic waʿada use the root of promising and of appointing a time and place, and their mawʿid, mwʿd, is an appointed time.

words.gloss: appointed time; appointed feast; meeting, meeting place

senses.definition: A time fixed beforehand, by Yahweh or by agreement, at which something is to happen.

evidence.note: Yahweh will return at the מוֹעֵד, and Sarah will have a son.
Sarah bears Isaac at the מוֹעֵד of which God had spoken.
Saul waits seven days for the מוֹעֵד Samuel had set, and Samuel does not come.
Amasa is later than the מוֹעֵד the king had appointed (יְעָדוֹ) him.
Yahweh sets a מוֹעֵד: tomorrow.
The vision is still for the מוֹעֵד; it will surely come.
The vision is for the מוֹעֵד of the end.
לְמוֹעֵד מוֹעֲדִים וָחֵצִי, a set time, set times and a half.
Parallel to עֵת: it is time to favour Zion, for the מוֹעֵד has come.
Paul quotes Gen 18:14 as the word of promise.
Hebrews quotes Hab 2:3 of the coming one, who will come and not delay.

senses.definition: The recurring times of the year, which the lights mark and which animals and crops keep.

evidence.note: The lights are for signs, for מוֹעֲדִים, and for days and years.
He made the moon for מוֹעֲדִים.
The stork knows her מוֹעֲדִים; parallel to the עֵת of the birds' coming.
My wine in its מוֹעֵד, parallel to my grain in its עֵת.

senses.definition: The times Yahweh fixes for Israel to proclaim as holy convocations and keep before him with offerings: in Leviticus 23 the sabbath, פֶּסַח (Passover) and חַג הַמַּצּוֹת (the feast of unleavened bread), the first sheaf, the fiftieth day, the first of the seventh month, יוֹם הַכִּפֻּרִים (the day of coverings) and חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת (the feast of booths).

evidence.note: The מוֹעֲדֵי יַהְוֶה, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations: these are my מוֹעֲדִים.
Proclaimed each בְּמוֹעֲדָם, at its own set time.
The chapter's summary: these are Yahweh's מוֹעֲדִים, with their offerings, each on its day.
Moses declares the מוֹעֲדֵי יַהְוֶה to Israel.
Israel is to keep the פֶּסַח at its מוֹעֵד.
Yahweh's offering is to be brought at its מוֹעֵד.
Unleavened bread at the מוֹעֵד of the month of the Aviv.
Her feast, her new moon, her sabbath, all her מוֹעֵד.
Your new moons and your מוֹעֲדִים my soul hates.
Zion's roads mourn: none come to the מוֹעֵד.
The people come before Yahweh at the מוֹעֲדִים.
The fasts are to become joyful מוֹעֲדִים.
Sabbaths, new moons and מוֹעֲדִים.
Feast, new moon and sabbaths: Paul names the same set of times.

senses.definition: The meeting Yahweh appoints with his people, and in אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד the tent where he meets Moses and Israel and speaks with them.

evidence.note: The entrance of the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד, where I will meet (אִוָּעֵד) with you to speak to you there.
Moses calls the tent אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד, and all who seek Yahweh go out to it.
Moses goes into the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד to speak with him and hears the voice from above the כַּפֹּרֶת.
Yahweh speaks to Moses from the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד.
The עֵדָה gathers (נוֹעֲדוּ) at the entrance of the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד.
Stephen speaks of the tent of witness in the wilderness, the Greek name of the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד.

senses.definition: A place where people gather by appointment: the meeting places of God in the land, the mount of assembly the king of Babylon boasts he will sit on, and death as the house of meeting for all the living.

evidence.note: I will sit on the הַר מוֹעֵד, in the far north.
They burned all the מוֹעֲדֵי־אֵל in the land.
The enemies roar in the midst of your מוֹעֵד.
He destroyed his מוֹעֵד; Yahweh made מוֹעֵד and sabbath forgotten in Zion.
Death, the בֵּית מוֹעֵד for all the living.
קְרִאֵי מוֹעֵד, those called to the assembly, beside the leaders of the עֵדָה.

senses.definition: A sign agreed beforehand between two parties.

evidence.note: The מוֹעֵד between Israel and the ambush was a great cloud of smoke from the city.

evidence.locator: Gen.18.14, לַמּוֹעֵד → καιρὸν; Dan.12.7, לְמוֹעֵד מוֹעֲדִים → καιρὸν … καιροὺς; καιρός renders מוֹעֵד ×25

evidence.note: “At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son”, quoting Gen 18:14.
“A time, and times, and half a time”, the reckoning of Dan 12:7.

evidence.locator: Exo.33.7, אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד → σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου
evidence.note: The Greek names the tent as if from עוּד “witness”; the Hebrew's own use (Exo 29:42) names it for the meeting.

parallels.note: Set beside מוֹעֵד as the time of something.

words.summary: Those who have gathered together. Scripture's own use ties it to the verb: the עֵדָה gathers (נוֹעֲדוּ) at the tent of meeting (Num 10:3), and Korah's עֵדָה are “those gathered (הַנֹּעָדִים) against Yahweh” (Num 16:11; 27:3).

senses.definition: Israel as one body gathered before Yahweh, whom he addresses, counts and leads, and which acts, judges and is judged together.

evidence.note: At the trumpets all the עֵדָה gathers (וְנוֹעֲדוּ) at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Speak to all the עֲדַת יִשְׂרָאֵל: each man is to take a lamb.
Speak to all the עֲדַת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל: you shall be holy.
That the עֲדַת יַהְוֶה be not as sheep without a shepherd.
קְהַל עֲדַת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל, the assembly of the congregation.
The עֵדָה judges between the slayer and the avenger of blood.
The cities of appointment (מוּעָדָה), until the slayer stands before the עֵדָה.
In the council of the upright and the עֵדָה.

senses.definition: Any group gathered together, whether of the righteous, of evildoers, or of God's council; once a swarm of bees.

evidence.note: Korah and all his עֵדָה.
A עֲדַת of evildoers encircles me.
Sinners shall not stand in the עֲדַת of the righteous.
God stands in the עֲדַת־אֵל.
A עֲדַת of the violent seeks my life.
The עֲדַת of the godless is barren.
You have made desolate all my עֵדָה, of Job's household or company.
A עֲדַת of bees in the lion's carcass.

parallels.note: The assembly; joined with עֵדָה and set beside it.

evidence.note: In the midst of the קָהָל and the עֵדָה.

senses.definition: Set a person apart for someone, of a master designating a servant woman as wife for himself or his son.

evidence.note: Her master, who designated her for himself.
If he designates her for his son.

senses.gloss: appoint a time or a place
senses.definition: Fix the time or place at which someone is to act.

evidence.note: The מוֹעֵד that the king had appointed him.
Against Ashkelon and the sea coast, there Yahweh has appointed the sword.
Hear the rod, and who appointed it; the line is difficult.

senses.definition: Meet with someone at an agreed place, above all Yahweh meeting with Moses and Israel at the tent and the covering.

evidence.note: There I will meet with you and speak with you from above the כַּפֹּרֶת.
There I will meet with the sons of Israel, and it will be made holy by my glory.
Do two walk together unless they have met (נוֹעָדוּ)?
Come, let us meet together in the villages.
Let us meet in the house of God.

senses.definition: Come together as a body by arrangement, of Israel's leaders and congregation, of rebels against Yahweh, of kings for war, and of friends.

evidence.note: At one trumpet the leaders gather to you.
This evil congregation gathered against me.
You and all your congregation gathered against Yahweh.
All these kings met together and camped at the waters of Merom.
Job's three friends met together to come and comfort him.

senses.definition: Appoint someone a time to appear, as for a trial.

evidence.note: If it is a matter of justice, who will summon him?
Who is like me, and who will summon me?

senses.gloss: be set in place, be directed
senses.definition: Be placed at a fixed spot or turned toward a fixed direction.

evidence.note: Two baskets of figs set before the temple of Yahweh.
Wherever your face is directed.

words.summary: Once, in a hard line: “none stands apart in his מוֹעָדִים” (Isa 14:31), of the ranks of the host coming from the north, or of Philistia's gatherings. The form points to an appointed place; the verse alone does not fix it.

senses.definition: A place where one is set, in its one occurrence.

evidence.note: וְאֵין בּוֹדֵד בְּמוֹעָדָיו, none stands apart in his appointed places.

senses.definition: In עָרֵי הַמּוּעָדָה, the cities appointed as refuge for one who has killed by mistake.

evidence.note: These were the cities of appointment for all Israel and the sojourner.

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for the ἐκκλησία, the same word as Hebrew עֵדָה. It also stands for the קָהָל of Psa 22:23 where Hebrews quotes it.

senses.definition: The gathered people of God: the assembly Jesus builds and to which a dispute is brought, the body whose head is Christ.

evidence.note: On this rock I will build my עִדְתָּא.
Tell it to the עִדְתָּא; if he will not listen to the עִדְתָּא…
He is the head of the body, the עִדְתָּא.
The Lord added daily to the עִדְתָּא those being saved.
In the midst of the עִדְתָּא I will praise you, quoting Psa 22:23 (קָהָל).
The עִדְתָּא of the firstborn enrolled in heaven.

senses.definition: Fix the place where others are to come.

evidence.note: The eleven go to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them (דּוַעֵד אֵנֻון).

senses.definition: The place agreed on for meeting.

evidence.note: They sail לוַעדָּא, to the appointed meeting at Assos, to take Paul on board.

cognates.gloss: promise; (III) appoint with someone the time and the place; (VI) appoint mutually the place and the time
cognates.note: Arabic keeps the first w where Hebrew has y. The plain verb is to promise; with another party, to fix a time and place together, the niphal's meeting by arrangement.

evidence.note: وَاعَدَهُ الوَقْتَ والمَوْضِعَ “He appointed with him the time, and the place”; تَوَاعَدْنَا المَوْضِعَ “We appointed mutually the place, and the time”.

cognates.gloss: time and place of a promise or appointment; appointed time and place
cognates.note: The same m-noun as מוֹעֵד, naming both the time and the place appointed.

evidence.note: “A time, and a place, of promise: [and, of appointment; an appointed time, and place]”.

cognates.gloss: promise; (h-stem) make an appointment, summon at an appointed time
cognates.note: Sabaic. The causative summons people to meet at an appointed time (C 541/61–2, “he summoned them (to meet) in the month dS”), as the hiphil of יָעַד summons to a hearing.

evidence.note: “PROMISE [Ar waʿada id.]”; h: “MAKE AN APPOINTMENT, SUMMON AT AN APPOINTED TIME”.

cognates.gloss: time limit, deadline; appointed time; feast-day (?)
cognates.note: Sabaic, the same m-noun as מוֹעֵד. Biella's sense “feast-day” rests on one text (C 548/1, whoever visits a sanctuary on the mwʿd of a god) and is marked uncertain.

evidence.note: “(1) (TIME) LIMIT, DEADLINE; APPOINTED TIME > FEAST-DAY (?) [Ar mīʿād “time agreed on, deadline.”]”.

cognates.note: Segert compares Hebrew עֵדָה and Syriac ʿidtā.

evidence.note: “ʿdt 1.100:3 “assembly” (H. ʿēdā, Syr. ʿidtā)”.

cognates.gloss: fixed date, appointed time, deadline, term
cognates.note: The meaning matches מוֹעֵד “appointed time”, but Akkadian a- does not show which first consonant stood behind it, so a tie to this root is argued, not shown.

evidence.note: Senses: “appointed time”, “appropriate time”, “deadline”, “fixed date”, “fixed time”, “period”, “term”.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh names the tent for what he does there: at its entrance, over the continual burnt offering, “I will meet (אִוָּעֵד) with you to speak to you there; there I will meet with the sons of Israel, and it will be made holy by my glory”, and he will dwell among them and be their God (Exo 29:42–46). The meeting is at the כַּפֹּרֶת, the covering over the box of the testimony, between the cherubim (Exo 25:22), and from there Moses hears the voice speaking to him (Num 7:89). Everyone who sought Yahweh went out to the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד (Exo 33:7). Hebrews calls that covering the ἱλαστήριον (Heb 9:5), and Paul says God set forth Christ Jesus as the ἱλαστήριον through faith in his blood (Rom 3:25). Christ came as high priest through the greater and more perfect tent, not made with hands, and entered the holy place once for all by his own blood (Heb 9:11–12); so believers have boldness to enter by his blood and are told to draw near (Heb 10:19–22). Read together, these verses put the meeting the tent was named for in Christ.

Leviticus 23 begins by saying whose the times are: “the מוֹעֲדֵי יַהְוֶה, which you shall proclaim as holy convocations, these are my מוֹעֲדִים” (Lev 23:2), and ends with Moses declaring the מוֹעֲדֵי יַהְוֶה to Israel (Lev 23:44). They are kept by the lights God made for מוֹעֲדִים (Gen 1:14; Psa 104:19). When Israel kept them as its own, Yahweh spoke of “her feast, her new moon, her sabbath and all her מוֹעֵד” and said he would end them (Hos 2:13), and of “your new moons and your מוֹעֲדִים”, which his soul hates (Isa 1:14). Paul names the same set, feast, new moon and sabbaths, and says no one is to judge believers in them: they are a shadow of what was to come, but the body is Christ's (Col 2:16–17). The New Testament sets Christ's death, his resurrection and the gift of the Spirit at the times the chapter appoints: Christ our פֶּסַח (Passover) has been sacrificed (1Co 5:7; Lev 23:5); the risen Christ is the firstfruits (1Co 15:20, 23), the name of the first sheaf of the harvest brought to Yahweh (Lev 23:10–11); and the Spirit is poured out when the day of Pentecost, the fiftieth day, has come (Act 2:1–4; Lev 23:15–16).

What Yahweh fixes for a מוֹעֵד happens at it. He tells Abraham, “at the מוֹעֵד I will return to you, and Sarah will have a son” (Gen 18:14), and she bears him “at the מוֹעֵד of which God had spoken” (Gen 21:2); Paul quotes it as the word of promise (Rom 9:9). Habakkuk is told that the vision is still for the מוֹעֵד: if it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come; and the righteous will live by his faithfulness (Hab 2:3–4). Hebrews reads this of the coming one, who will come and not delay, and calls believers to endure and live by faith (Heb 10:36–38). Daniel is shown that the end is for the מוֹעֵד (Dan 8:19; 11:35). Waiting for Yahweh's מוֹעֵד is trusting his word.

note: Left out: the names נוֹעַדְיָה and יֶעְדּוֹ (name entries). עֵד “witness”, עֵדוּת “testimony” and the verb הֵעִיד belong to עוּד, though the Greek renders אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד as “tent of witness”; BDB's key j.cb.ab for עֵדָה also takes in Gen 31:52, where עֵדָה is “witness” (fem. of עֵד, under עוּד), so its use count is one too high. עֵת “time” is left out: Phoenician ʿt and Aramaic כְּעֶנֶת point to ʿnt, not this root. Biblical Aramaic עִדָּן “time” (Dan 7:25) is a different spelling (ʿdn) with no shown tie to יעד. The Peshitta's feast word (ܥܐܕܐ, ܥܕܥܕܐ, e.g. Col 2:16, 1Co 5:8) is root ʿyd, a different root. Open: (1) the Syriac verb's stem is read as pael from SEDRA's vocalisation OaEeD (waʿed); SEDRA lexemes 830–831, 2255; Payne Smith and Brockelmann not consulted for ܘܥܕ or ܥܕܬܐ. (2) Biella p. 134 was read from the scan's OCR text only (no PDF renderer here); check the diacritics and page on the scan. (3) Ugaritic mʿd “assembly” (as הַר מוֹעֵד) was not found in the vendored Segert or Fisher; check a fuller Ugaritic dictionary. (4) Mic 6:9 and Isa 14:31 are difficult lines. (5) CAL and Old Aramaic not consulted; Jewish Aramaic יְעַד (Pa. “designate”) and Targumic מוֹעֲדָא (Targ. Lev 23:2) are in Jastrow but may echo the Hebrew, so are not recorded as cognates. (6) Doctrine: the Lev 23 links to 1Co 15:20 and Act 2:1 rest on the New Testament's naming (firstfruits, Pentecost), not on an explicit citation of Lev 23; review.
